public_text.9:
From the ionisation current the power which is actually absorbed in the
air which is in the beam is

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W_{air}/e$

$W_{air}/e\simeq33.97\,{\rm V}$ for air.  With $I=2.0\times10^{-12}{\rm A}$

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\approx6.7\!-\!6.8\times10^{-11}\,
{\rm W}$

in the volume which is intersected by the 0.30$\times$6.0 mm$^{2}$ focus.

The geometrical mass of air which is seen by the beam in the chamber is

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.80\times10^{-2}\,
{\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L_{c}=1.80\times10^{-2}\times15.1=0.272\;{\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}{\rm g\,cm^{-3}}\times0.272\;{\rm
cm^{3}}\approx3.5\times10^{-4}{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}{\rm kg}$ .

Hence the instantaneous air kerma, and with $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq
(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$ the tissue absorbed dose rate, in the focal spot is

$\dot K_{a}=\dot D_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}
       =\dfrac{I\,W/e}{\rho_{a}A_{f}L_{c}}
       \approx\dfrac{6.8\times10^{-11}}{3.5\times10^{-7}}
       \approx1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

$\approx0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in soft tissue at the entrance of the chamber.  With $k_{en}=
(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho =0.328\times1.293\times10^{-3}=4.24\times10^{-4}{\rm
cm^{-1}}$ $k_{en}L_{c}\simeq6\times10^{-3}\ll1$ so that attenuation in the
15.1 cm of air is negligible and the quoted $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328
{\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$ is a consistency check only.

A surface element stays in the $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal fan for the
dwell

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}=w_{f}/\bigl({\rm scan\,step}/{t_{exp}}\bigr)\approx
2.0\times10^{-2}\ {\rm s}$,

the number quoted in the statement.  The dose received by that element on
one monochromatic pass is therefore

$D_{1}= \dot D_{t}\,t_{d}\approx1.93\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}
      \times2.0\times10^{-2}\ {\rm s}\approx3.5\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}$

$\approx3\!-\!4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per 20 ms projection, $ \approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$
with $W_{air}=33.97\;{\rm eV}$.  This is the familiar $\approx0.19\,{\rm
mGy\,s^{-1}}$ peak air/tissue kerma rate times the 20 ms dwell normally
quoted for the 33 keV Laue focus.

The dose scales linearly with the number of energies used in the
multi-energy acquisition,

$D_{N}=N\,D_{1}$,

e.g. $D_{2}\approx7\!-\!8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ for the conventional dual-energy
Laue acquisition and $D_{3}\approx11\!-\!12\;\mu{\rm Gy}$, $\approx
1.2\times10^{-5}\ {\rm Gy}$, for a three-energy material decomposition
set, per scanned point.  In the often quoted $ {\rm mGy}$ form this is
$\approx3.9\times10^{-3}\ {\rm mGy}$ per energy per point.

If the dose is summed over the whole $W_{i}=50\ {\rm mm}$ Laue-dispersed
field which is mapped by the $w_{f}=0.30\ {\rm mm}$ spot,

$N_{h}\simeq W_{i}/w_{f}\approx50/0.30\approx1.67\times10^{2}$,

the kerma integrated over the $50\,{\rm mm}\times6\,{\rm mm}$ scanned
line per energy is

$D_{int}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\approx1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm
Gy}\approx6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$,

$\approx0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, per monochromatic
energy band.  The mean dose averaged over the $W_{i}$ field is
$D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}\approx20\!-\!30\ {\rm
nGy}$ per energy, i.e. the $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per point, $\sim0.19\ {\rm
mGy\,s^{-1}}$ instantaneous, $\sim0.6\ {\rm mGy}$ field-integrated values
normally quoted for synchrotron multiple-energy micro-beam imaging. ∎
public_text.11:
The ionisation current is the power which is taken out of the beam in the
air which is at any instant in the focal spot.

$W_{air}\simeq 33.97\;{\rm eV}$ per ion pair so that

$\dot E_{abs}=I\,W/e$

is the power absorbed in the air which is illuminated.  With
$I=2.0\times10^{-12}{\rm A}$

$\dot E_{abs}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\approx6.8\times10^{-11}\;{\rm 
W}$

is absorbed in the volume which is seen by the focus.  The mass of air
which is seen at any instant is

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.80\times10^{-2}\,
{\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.80\times10^{-2}\times15.1=0.272\;{\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}= \rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\approx3.5\times10^{-4}
\;{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}\;{\rm kg}$

so that the instantaneous air kerma rate in the $0.30\times6.0\;{\rm
mm^{2}}$ focal spot is

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{abs}/m_{a}
      =I\,W/e\,/\,m_{a}
      \approx 6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}
      \approx1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\;{\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

$\approx0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$ in air and, with
$(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$ at 33 keV, the same
absorbed dose rate in soft tissue at the focus.  The $k_{en}L$ in 15.1 cm
of air is $k_{en}L=(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho L\approx6.4\times10^{-3}\ll1$ so

the dwell quoted in the statement.  The kerma, i.e. the absorbed dose,

i.e.

$D_{1}\simeq3.9\times10^{-6}\;{\rm Gy}\approx3\!-\!4\;\mu{\rm Gy}\approx
0.004\;{\rm mGy}$

per 20 ms dwell per monochromatic channel, $\approx0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$
peak at the focus, essentially independent of the $(\mu_{en}/\rho)$

$D_{int}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\approx1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}
      \approx6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\;{\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\;{\rm mGy}$

per energy channel to the $50\times6\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ scanned surface,

nGy}$ mean dose averaged over the whole $50\,{\rm mm}$ field per energy.

surface dose quoted for the synchrotron multiple energy scan; the

In an air ionisation chamber

which energy is put into the mass of air which is actually seen by the
beam.  With $W/e\simeq33.97\ {\rm V}$ for air

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}{\rm A}\times33.97\ {\rm V}\approx6.8\times
10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$

in the volume which is illuminated at the focus.  At the focus

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.8\times10^{-2}{\rm
cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L_{c}=1.8\times10^{-2}\times15.1=0.272\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}{\rm g\,cm^{-3}}\times0.272{\rm
cm^{3}}\approx3.5\times10^{-4}{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}{\rm kg}$,

so that the instantaneous air kerma rate in the $0.30\times6.0\,{\rm mm^{2}}$
focal spot is

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}\approx
6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}\approx1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

$\approx0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$ in air.

$k_{en}=(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho=0.328\times1.293\times10^{-3}=4.24\times10^{-4}
{\rm cm^{-1}}$, $k_{en}L\simeq6.4\times10^{-3}\ll1$, so the entrance
kerma is essentially the mean kerma in the $15.1\,{\rm cm}$ air column.
With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$ at $33\;{\rm keV}$ the
same rate is the absorbed dose rate in soft tissue at the focal plane,

$\dot D_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\approx1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$ .

A surface element which is carried through the $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$
horizontal fan stays in the beam for the dwell

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v=w_{f}/(\Delta x/t_{exp})\approx2.0\times10^{-2}\ {\rm s}$

as quoted.  The dose actually delivered to a surface element on one
monochromatic pass through the fan is therefore

$D_{1}=\dot D_{t}t_{d}\approx1.93\times10^{-4}{\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\times
2.0\times10^{-2}{\rm s}\approx3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}$

per energy step, i.e.

$D_{1}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}\approx3.9\times10^{-3}\ {\rm mGy}$

per $20\;{\rm ms}$ dwell $\approx0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$ peak air–tissue
kerma rate at the focus.  In energy fluence form
$\dot K=\Phi E(\mu_{en}/\rho)$ this is
$\Phi\approx1\times10^{8}\ {\rm ph\,cm^{-2}s^{-1}}$ at $33\;{\rm keV}$,
$(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\;{\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$.

material decomposition.  The conventional dual–energy Laue acquisition is
$D_{2E}\simeq2D_{1}\approx7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx7.8\;\mu{\rm
Gy}$ per scanned point and $3D_{1}\approx11\!-\!12\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ for a
three energy set, i.e. a few $\mu{\rm Gy}$ per image point, the
$\approx4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per 20 ms dwell being the peak surface kerma
normally quoted for the 2.0 pA, 33 keV focus.

If the dose is summed over the whole Laue dispersed field which is
covered by scanning the $0.30\;{\rm mm}$ focus over the $W_{i}=50\;{\rm mm}$
monochromator illumination, $N_{h}=W_{i}/w_{f}\approx50/0.30\approx1.67\times
10^{2}$ independent horizontal positions are visited.  The kerma
integrated over the $50\;{\rm mm}\times6\;{\rm mm}$ scanned line per
energy channel is

$D_{int}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\approx1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
\approx6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$,

$\approx0.64\;{\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, $\approx0.64\;{\rm mGy}$
surface air kerma for the complete $50\;{\rm mm}$ Laue fan per energy
channel.  The mean dose averaged over the $50\times6\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ field
is $D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}{\rm Gy}\approx20\!-\!30\;{\rm nGy}$
per energy, the familiar $\sim 4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per dwell being the local
peak surface dose under the $0.30\times6.0\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ focal spot.
The $0.6\;{\rm mGy}$ integrated figure is $N_{E}D_{int}$ for $N_{E}$
distinct energies. ∎

$D_{int}\simeq N_h D_1\approx1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}

Ḋ_air = Ė / m_air ≈6.8×10⁻¹¹ /3.5×10⁻⁷ ≈1.9–2.0×10⁻⁴ Gy s⁻¹ ≈0.19 mGy s⁻¹

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The ionisation current is converted to an air power $\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$ with $W/e\simeq33.97\;{\rm V}$ for air,

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\approx6.7\!-\!6.8\times10^{-11}\,{\rm W}$,

absorbed in the instantaneous mass in the focus

$A_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.8\times10^{-2}\,{\rm cm^{2}}$,
$V_{f}=A_{f}L=0.272\,{\rm cm^{3}}$, 
$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\approx3.5\times10^{-4}{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}{\rm kg}$.

Hence

$\dot K_{a}=\dot E_{a}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/\rho_{a}A_{f}L\approx6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}\approx1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\,{\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\approx0.19\,{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air. With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\,{\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$ at 33 keV this is taken as the absorbed dose rate in soft tissue at the focus. $k_{en}L=(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho L\approx6.4\times10^{-3}\ll1$, so attenuation in the 15.1 cm air column is negligible.

A surface element stays in the $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal fan for the quoted dwell

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}=w_{f}/[{\rm scan\;step}/{\rm exp\;time}]\simeq0.020\,{\rm s}$.

The peak surface dose deposited in that element on one monochromatic passage, i.e. one energy step, is

$D_{1}= \dot D_{t}t_{d}\approx1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}\approx3.5\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\,{\rm Gy}\approx3.9\,\mu{\rm Gy}\approx3.9\times10^{-3}\,{\rm mGy}$

per 20 ms dwell per energy, essentially independent of $(\mu_{en}/\rho)$ under the tissue≈air approximation. This is the $ \sim4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy per point level repeatedly quoted by Colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12,13,14,15 in both rounds. The instantaneous peak rate is $\approx0.19\,{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$.

Dose is additive with the number of energies $N_{E}$ used: $D_{N_{E}}\approx N_{E}D_{1}$, e.g. $\approx7\!-\!8\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ for a conventional dual-energy Laue set and $\approx11\!-\!12\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ for three energies per scanned point.

Geometrical dilution. The $50\,{\rm mm}$ incident horizontal width is compressed to $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ at focus,

$N_{h}=W_{i}/w_{f}\approx50/0.30\approx1.67\times10^{2}$ independent horizontal positions.

Integrated over the whole $50\times6\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ scanned line per monochromatic energy,

$D_{int}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\approx1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\approx6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\,{\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\,{\rm mGy}\approx0.64\,{\rm mGy}$

per energy, $N_{h}t_{d}\approx3.3\,{\rm s}$ total dwell. The mean dose averaged over the whole field is $D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\,{\rm Gy}\approx20\!-\!30\,{\rm nGy}$ per energy, $\approx46\,{\rm nGy}$ for dual energy.

Colleague 7 remains the outlier interpreting the quoted $0.02\,{\rm s}$ ratio as a multiplier of the exposure time, $t_{d}=0.02\times0.02\,{\rm s}=4\times10^{-4}\,{\rm s}$, giving $\sim7\!-\!8\times10^{-8}\,{\rm Gy}$, and is not followed by the majority. All other colleagues converge on $\dot D\approx1.9\times10^{-4}\,{\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$ and $D_{1}\approx3\!-\!4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy dwell.

Unresolved for the present question is the exact definition of “cumulative”: per-point per-energy $ \approx3.9\,\mu{\rm Gy}$, per-point total $N_{E}D_{1}$ $\sim7\!-\!8\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ for dual energy, or field-integrated $\sim0.64\,{\rm mGy}$ per energy over the 50 mm Laue fan. The $50\,{\rm mm}$ incident size does not change the local point dose; it only sets the $N_{h}\approx167$ scan dilution and the integrated/mean-over-field numbers.

dose rate in soft tissue, in the $0.30\times6.0\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ focal spot
is

$\dot K_{a}=\dot D_{t}\simeq\dot E_{a}/m_{a}
     =\dfrac{I\,W/e}{\rho_{a}A_{f}L}
     \simeq\dfrac{6.8\times10^{-11}}{3.5\times10^{-7}}
     \simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

$\approx0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$ peak in the focus. 
$k_{en}L=(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho L\simeq6.4\times10^{-3}\ll1$ so the $15.1\;{\rm cm}$
air column is essentially non–absorbing and the entrance kerma is the mean
kerma.

A surface element stays in the $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ horizontal fan for

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}\simeq2.0\times10^{-2}{\rm s}$

the dwell quoted in the statement.  The peak surface kerma, i.e. the
absorbed dose to the surface layer of tissue, deposited in that element
on one monochromatic passage of the Laue spot is therefore

$D_{1}= \dot D_{t}\,t_{d}
      \simeq1.93\times10^{-4}{\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\times2.0\times10^{-2}{\rm s}
      \simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}{\rm Gy}$

$D_{1}\simeq3.9\,\mu{\rm Gy}\approx3.9\times10^{-3}{\rm mGy}$ per $20\,{\rm ms}$
dwell per monochromatic energy step, $0.19\,{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times0.02\,{\rm s}$,
the usual $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection synchrotron micro-beam
level.  With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$ the same number
is the tissue absorbed dose.

The dose is additive with the number of energies used in the Laue
multi-energy acquisition, $D_{N_{E}}\simeq N_{E}D_{1}$,
e.g.

$D_{2E}\simeq2D_{1}\approx7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}{\rm Gy}\approx7.8\,\mu{\rm Gy}$
per scanned point for the conventional dual-energy set and
$D_{3E}\simeq3D_{1}\approx1.1\!-\!1.2\times10^{-5}{\rm Gy}\approx11\!-\!12\,
\mu{\rm Gy}$ per point for a three-energy material decomposition set.

If the energy is summed over the whole $W_{i}=50\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal
field which is covered by scanning the $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ focus,
$N_{h}=W_{i}/w_{f}\simeq50/0.30\approx1.67\times10^{2}$ independent
positions are required, $N_{h}t_{d}\simeq3.3\,{\rm s}$ total dwell per
energy.  The integrated surface kerma over the $50\times6\,{\rm mm^{2}}$
scanned line per monochromatic view is

$D_{int}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}{\rm Gy}
      \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}{\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\,{\rm mGy}$,

$\approx0.64\,{\rm mGy}$ surface air/tissue kerma to the complete
$50\,{\rm mm}$ Laue fan per energy, i.e. $D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}
{\rm Gy}\approx20\!-\!30\,{\rm nGy}$ mean dose averaged over the whole
$50\times6\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ field per energy.  The $\approx4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$
per $20\,{\rm ms}$ dwell is the local peak surface dose normally quoted
for the system; it scales linearly with $N_{E}$ for a multi-energy
acquisition. ∎

8.text:
The power which is registered in the air of the chamber is the power
which is taken out of the beam in the air which is at the instant in the
beam

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$ ,  $W/e\simeq 33.97\,{\rm V}$ for air

$$
\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}{\rm A}\times33.97{\rm V}\simeq
6.7\!-\!6.8\times10^{-11}{\rm W}
$$

in the volume which is illuminated at the focus.  At the focus

$$
A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30{\rm mm}\times6.0{\rm mm}=1.80\times10^{-2}{\rm 
cm^{2}}
$$

$$
V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.80\times10^{-2}\times15.1=0.272{\rm cm^{3}}
$$

$$
m_{a}= \rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}{\rm g\,cm^{-3}}\times0.272{\rm
cm^{3}}\simeq3.5\times10^{-4}{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}{\rm kg}
$$

is the mass of air which is in the beam at any instant.  Hence the
instantaneous air kerma in the $0.30\times6.0\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ focal spot
and, with $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$ at 33 keV, the
instantaneous absorbed dose rate in soft tissue at the focus is

$$
\dot K_{a}=\dot D_{t}\simeq\frac{\dot E_{a}}{m_{a}}=
\frac{I\,W/e}{\rho_{a}A_{f}L}
      \simeq\frac{6.8\times10^{-11}}{3.5\times10^{-7}}
      \simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}
$$

i.e.

$$
\dot D_{t}\simeq0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}
$$

in the instantaneous focal spot.  $k_{en}L=(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho L\simeq
0.328\times1.293\times10^{-3}\times15.1\simeq6.4\times10^{-3}\ll1$ so
that the $15.1\,{\rm cm}$ air column is essentially non-absorbing and
the entrance kerma can be used for the tissue dose.  In fluence form

$\dot D_{t}= \Phi E_{0}(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}$ this is $\Phi\sim10^{12}\,
{\rm m^{-2}s^{-1}}$ at $33\,{\rm keV}$.

A surface element stays in the $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal fan for

$$
t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}=w_{f}/\bigl[\Delta x/t_{exp}\bigr]\simeq2.0\times10^{-2}
{\rm s}
$$

the dwell quoted in the statement.  The surface kerma, i.e. the absorbed
dose to the surface layer of tissue, deposited in that element on one
monochromatic passage of the Laue spot is therefore

$$
D_{1}= \dot D_{t}\,t_{d}\simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}
       \times2.0\times10^{-2}\ {\rm s}
       \simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy},
$$

$$
D_{1}\simeq3.9\times10^{-6}{\rm Gy}\approx3\!-\!4\;\mu{\rm Gy}
      \approx3.9\times10^{-3}{\rm mGy}
$$

per 20 ms dwell per monochromatic energy channel, 
$\dot D_{t}\approx0.19\,{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times0.020\,{\rm s}$, essentially
independent of the quoted $(\mu_{en}/\rho)$ under the
$(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\approx(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$ approximation.  This is
the $\sim4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection peak surface dose normally quoted
for a $33\,{\rm keV}$, $2.0\,{\rm pA}$ Laue micro-beam.

The dose is additive with the number of energies used in the Laue
acquisition, $D_{N_{E}}\simeq N_{E}D_{1}$.  In particular

* $N_{E}=2\;:$ $D_{2}\simeq2D_{1}\approx7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}{\rm Gy}
\approx7.8\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per scanned point,
* $N_{E}=3\;:$ $D_{3}\simeq3D_{1}\approx1.1\!-\!1.2\times10^{-5}{\rm Gy}
\approx11\!-\!12\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per scanned point,

the familiar few $\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection synchrotron level.

If the energy is summed over the whole $W_{i}=50\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal
Laue fan which is mapped to the $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ focus,

$$
N_{h}=W_{i}/w_{f}\simeq50/0.30\approx1.67\times10^{2}
$$

independent horizontal positions are visited, $N_{h}t_{d}\simeq3.3\,{\rm s}$
total dwell per energy.  The kerma integrated over the $50\,{\rm mm}
\times6\,{\rm mm}$ scanned line per monochromatic energy is

$$
D_{\rm int}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}
{\rm Gy}\simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}{\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7{\rm mGy},
$$

$\approx0.64\,{\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, i.e. 
$\approx D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}{\rm Gy}\approx
20\!-\!30\,{\rm nGy}$ mean dose averaged over the whole $50\times6\,
{\rm mm^{2}}$ field per energy.  This $ \sim0.6\,{\rm mGy}$ is the
field-integrated surface air/tissue kerma that a point receives while
transiting the complete $50\,{\rm mm}$ Laue fan, $D_{\rm int}\approx
\dot D_{t}N_{h}t_{d}$, and $N_{E}D_{\rm int}$ for $N_{E}$ distinct
energies.  The $3\!-\!4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per 20 ms dwell is the local peak
surface dose per energy normally quoted for the multiple-energy
micro-imaging system. ∎

3.text:
In the chamber the ionisation current is the power which is taken out of
the beam in the mass of air which is at the instant in the focus

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$ ,  $W/e\simeq 33.97\;{\rm V}$ for air

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}{\rm A}\times33.97{\rm V}
          \simeq 6.7\!-\!6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$

is absorbed in the air which is seen by the focused beam.  At the
focus

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.80\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$

$V_{f}=A_{f}L =1.80\times10^{-2}\times15.1=0.272\ {\rm cm^{3}}$

$m_{a}= \rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}{\rm g\,cm^{-3}}\times0.272{\rm cm^{3}}
      \simeq3.5\times10^{-4}{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}{\rm kg}$

is the mass of air which is ionised at any instant. Hence the
instantaneous air kerma and, with $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq
(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$, the absorbed dose rate in soft tissue in the
$0.30\times6.0\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ focal spot is

$\dot K_{a}\simeq\dot D_{t}= \dfrac{\dot E_{a}}{m_{a}}
   =\dfrac{I\,W/e}{\rho_{a}A_{f}L}
   \simeq\dfrac{6.8\times10^{-11}}{3.5\times10^{-7}}
   \simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$

$\approx 0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$  peak at the focus.  In the
$\dot D=\Phi E(\mu_{en}/\rho)$ form

$k_{en}L=(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho L
       =0.328\times1.293\times10^{-3}\times15.1\simeq6.4\times10^{-3}\ll1$

so that the entrance kerma is essentially the mean kerma in the
15.1 cm air column and the quoted $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\;{\rm
cm^{2}g^{-1}}$ cancels in the $I\to{\rm dose}$ conversion.

A surface element stays in the $w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ horizontal fan for

$t_{d}=w_{f}/v_{s}=w_{f}/[\Delta x/t_{exp}]\simeq2.0\times10^{-2}\ {\rm s}$

the dwell quoted in the statement. The peak surface dose deposited in
that element on one monochromatic passage of the Laue spot is

$D_{1}= \dot D_{t}t_{d}
     \simeq1.93\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\times2.0\times10^{-2}\ {\rm s}
     \simeq3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}$

$D_{1}\simeq3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}\approx3.9\times10^{-3}{\rm mGy}$
per 20 ms dwell per monochromatic energy at the $0.30\times6.0\,{\rm
mm^{2}}$ focus, i.e. $0.19\,{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times0.020\,{\rm s}$,
the familiar $\sim4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per projection synchrotron
micro-beam level.  The dose is additive with the number of energies
used for material decomposition,

$D_{N_{E}}\simeq N_{E}D_{1}$ ,

e.g. $D_{2E}\simeq2D_{1}\approx7\!-\!8\times10^{-6}{\rm Gy}\approx
7.8\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per point for the usual dual-energy Laue acquisition
and $D_{3E}\simeq3D_{1}\approx1.1\!-\!1.2\times10^{-5}{\rm Gy}\approx
11\!-\!12\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per point for a three energy set.  This is the
local peak surface air/tissue kerma normally quoted for the 33 keV,
2.0 pA Laue focus.

The $50\,{\rm mm}$ monochromator illumination is compressed to the
$w_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}$ focus, $N_{h}=W_{i}/w_{f}=50/0.30\simeq1.67\times10^{2}$
independent horizontal positions.  Integrated over the whole
$50\times6\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ scanned Laue fan the kerma per monochromatic
channel is

$D_{int}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\simeq1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}{\rm Gy}
       \simeq6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}{\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$,

$\approx0.64\;{\rm mGy}$ surface air kerma for the complete 50 mm line
per energy, $N_{h}t_{d}\simeq3.3\;{\rm s}$ total dwell. The mean dose
averaged over the $50\times6\,{\rm mm^{2}}$ field is
$\langle D\rangle_{1}=D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}{\rm Gy}
\approx20\!-\!30\,{\rm nGy}$ per energy, the $ \sim4\,\mu{\rm Gy}$ per
20 ms dwell being the conventional local peak surface dose under the
focal spot. ∎

public_text.7:
The air kerma rate at the focus follows directly from the ionisation current and is the same for all of us.

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$ with $W/e\simeq33.97\;{\rm V}$ for air

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}{\rm A}\times33.97{\rm V}\approx6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$

The mass of air which is instantaneously in the $0.30\times6.0\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ focus in the $L=15.1\;{\rm cm}$ chamber is

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.80\times10^{-2}{\rm cm^{2}}$

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}A_{f}L=1.293\times10^{-3}{\rm g\,cm^{-3}}\times1.80\times10^{-2}{\rm cm^{2}}\times15.1{\rm cm}\approx3.5\times10^{-4}{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}{\rm kg}$

so that

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}\approx6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}\approx1.9\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\approx0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

in air. With $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}=0.328\;{\rm cm^{2}g^{-1}}$ at 33 keV this is the absorbed dose rate in soft tissue at the focal plane,
$\dot D_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}$, $k_{en}L\approx6\times10^{-3}\ll1$.

A surface element stays in the $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ horizontal fan for the quoted dwell

$t_{d}=0.020\;{\rm s}$

hence the local peak dose deposited in one monochromatic passage at a fixed point is

$D_{1}= \dot D_{t}t_{d}\approx1.93\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\times2.0\times10^{-2}\ {\rm s}\approx3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$

per energy per dwell, $ \approx0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times0.02\;{\rm s}$, the familiar $\sim4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per point figure.

That $D_{1}$ is the instantaneous peak under the 0.30 mm spot. The tissue that is imaged is not a single point, it is the $W_{i}=50\;{\rm mm}\times6\;{\rm mm}$ field that is covered by scanning the focus horizontally across the beam. The number of independent beam positions required to cover the monochromator illumination is

$N_{h}=W_{i}/w_{f}\approx50.0/0.30\approx1.67\times10^{2}$

so the total time the scanned line spends in the beam per energy is $N_{h}t_{d}\approx3.3\;{\rm s}$.

The cumulative surface energy put into the whole imaged $50\times6\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ line on one monochromatic pass is therefore the sum over the scan

$D_{cum}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\approx1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}$

$\approx6.4\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$ surface air/tissue kerma to the complete $50\;{\rm mm}$ Laue band per energy channel. This is $D_{1}$ integrated over the field, i.e. $N_{h}D_{1}$, with the mean dose averaged over the $50\;{\rm mm}$ field being $D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}\approx20\!-\!30\;{\rm nGy}$ per energy.

The $\approx3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}$ value is the local peak per point per dwell. The cumulative surface dose delivered to the tissue that is actually imaged, i.e. to the whole $50\;{\rm mm}\times6\;{\rm mm}$ scanned line, is the spatially integrated $\sim0.6\;{\rm mGy}$ per monochromatic energy, $\approx0.64\;{\rm mGy}$ with the nominal numbers, which scales as $N_{E}D_{cum}$ for $N_{E}$ energies in the multiple energy acquisition.

The ionisation current analysis that Colleagues 1,10,12,14,2,3,4,5,6,8,9 have laid out is the correct starting point and the numbers are now fixed in the discussion.

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$, $W/e\simeq33.97\;{\rm V}$ for air,

$\dot E_{a}=2.0\times10^{-12}\times33.97\approx6.8\times10^{-11}\ {\rm W}$

in the mass of air that is instantaneously in the beam. At the focus

$A_{f}=w_{f}h_{f}=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.80\times10^{-2}\ {\rm cm^{2}}$,

$V_{f}=A_{f}L=1.80\times10^{-2}\times15.1=0.272\ {\rm cm^{3}}$,

$m_{a}=\rho_{a}V_{f}=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\approx3.5\times10^{-4}\ {\rm g}
=3.5\times10^{-7}\ {\rm kg}$.

Hence the instantaneous air-kerma rate in the $0.30\times6.0\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ focal spot is

$\dot K_{a}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}=I\,W/e/m_{a}\approx6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}
\approx1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\approx0.19\ {\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$.

$k_{en}L=(\mu_{en}/\rho)\rho L\approx0.328\times1.293\times10^{-3}\times15.1
\approx6.4\times10^{-3}\ll1$, so the entrance kerma is essentially the mean
kerma in the chamber and with $(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{t}\simeq(\mu_{en}/\rho)_{a}$
the same rate is the absorbed dose rate in soft tissue at the focus,

$\dot D_{t}\simeq\dot K_{a}\approx1.93\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}$.

A surface element stays in the $w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ horizontal fan for the
quoted dwell

$t_{d}=0.020\ {\rm s}$,

so the local peak dose deposited in one monochromatic passage is

$D_{1}= \dot D_{t}t_{d}\approx1.93\times10^{-4}\times2.0\times10^{-2}
\approx3.8\!-\!4.0\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}\approx3.9\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per energy per
20 ms dwell.

That is the $ \approx4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ per-point per-energy figure that is
unanimously obtained above. It is the local peak surface kerma under the
focal spot, not the dose that is accumulated by the tissue that is actually
imaged.

The tissue that is imaged is the $W_{i}=50\;{\rm mm}\times6\;{\rm mm}$ field
that is illuminated at the monochromator and mapped by the Laue crystal into the
$w_{f}=0.30\;{\rm mm}$ focus. The number of independent horizontal beam
positions required to cover the monochromator illumination is

i.e. $N_{h}t_{d}\simeq3.3\ {\rm s}$ total dwell per energy over the line.
The energy that is put into the whole scanned $50\times6\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ line
on one monochromatic pass is therefore the per-point dose summed over the scan,

$D_{cum}\simeq N_{h}D_{1}\approx1.67\times10^{2}\times3.9\times10^{-6}\ {\rm Gy}
\approx6\!-\!7\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\approx0.6\!-\!0.7\ {\rm mGy}$,

$\approx6.4\times10^{-4}\ {\rm Gy}\approx0.64\ {\rm mGy}$ surface air/tissue
kerma to the complete $50\;{\rm mm}$ Laue fan per monochromatic energy.
The mean dose averaged over the whole $50\times6\;{\rm mm^{2}}$ field is
$D_{1}w_{f}/W_{i}\approx2\!-\!3\times10^{-8}\ {\rm Gy}\approx20\!-\!30\;{\rm nGy}$
per energy, the $3\!-\!4\;\mu{\rm Gy}$ being the local peak under the spot.

Power taken out of the beam in the air instantaneously in the focus

$\dot E_{a}=I\,W/e$, $W/e\simeq33.97\;{\rm V}$

Hence

$\dot K_{a}\simeq\dot D_{t}= \dot E_{a}/m_{a}\simeq6.8\times10^{-11}/3.5\times10^{-7}\simeq1.9\!-\!2.0\times10^{-4}{\rm Gy\,s^{-1}}\simeq0.19\,{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}$

$t_{d}=0.020\,{\rm s}$

the local peak dose deposited in a surface element on one monochromatic passage is

That $D_{1}$ is the single-energy, per-point component. The question asks for the cumulative surface dose to a tissue imaged using the multiple energy imaging system. per 20 ms dwell per monochromatic energy per scanned point,
$0.19\;{\rm mGy\,s^{-1}}\times0.020\;{\rm s}$,

$D_{N_{E}}=N_{E}D_{1}$,

e.g.

$\simeq0.64\;{\rm mGy}$ surface air/tissue kerma to the complete

$A_f=w_fh_f=0.30\,{\rm mm}\times6.0\,{\rm mm}=1.80\times10^{-2}{\rm cm^2}$,
$V_f=A_fL=1.80\times10^{-2}\times15.1=0.272\ {\rm cm^3}$,
$m_a=\rho_aV_f=1.293\times10^{-3}\times0.272\simeq3.5\times10^{-4}{\rm g}=3.5\times10^{-7}{\rm kg}$.

$W_i=50\ {\rm mm}$ incident monochromator width maps to $w_f=0.30\ {\rm mm}$,
